pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR contains several changes to allow users to fetch newly created dashboards and folders. 

The changes are:
* on client side: remove the use of authLib cache when running authZ service in-proc
* on server side: add a denial cache to return quickly when we know that a user does not have permission on a specific resource
* on server side: if permission denial cache is not hit, and the requested resource is not found in cached permissions, requery permissions from the DB

**Why do we need this feature?**

Otherwise dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana users

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/identity-access-team/issues/1316
pr.title: AuthZService: improve authz caching

raw_findings.body: The renderer's check hits the anonymous user's denial entry and is incorrectly denied even though getRendererPermissions grants a wildcard read, breaking dashboard rendering for up to the cache TTL.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A cached deny for one identity type is returned for a different identity type with the same UID, producing an incorrect authorization decision.
raw_findings.impact: The renderer's check hits the anonymous user's denial entry and is incorrectly denied even though getRendererPermissions grants a wildcard read, breaking dashboard rendering for up to the cache TTL.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new denial cache key is built only from namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent, while Check() serves identities of multiple types (user, service account, anonymous, renderer) whose UIDs can coincide.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include the identity type in userPermDenialCacheKey (e.g., pass checkReq.IdentityType and embed it in the key) so different identity types with equal UIDs cannot share denial entries.
raw_findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, causing cross-identity collisions (e.g., renderer vs anonymous)
raw_findings.trigger: Anonymous access is enabled; an anonymous request (subject "anonymous:0", parsed UserUID "0") is denied `dashboards:read` on dashboard X and the denial is cached. Within the 30s TTL, the render service (subject "render:0", also UserUID "0") checks `dashboards:read` on the same dashboard in the same namespace.

raw_findings.body: The second, unrelated resource check short-circuits to a cached deny, so a user can be incorrectly denied access to a resource they are actually permitted to see for up to the cache TTL.
raw_findings.evidence: return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cache key collision returns a denial result computed for a different resource, yielding wrong Check responses.
raw_findings.impact: The second, unrelated resource check short-circuits to a cached deny, so a user can be incorrectly denied access to a resource they are actually permitted to see for up to the cache TTL.
raw_findings.root_cause: Key components (name, parent) that can themselves contain the "_" separator are concatenated with "_", so distinct (name, parent) tuples can serialize to the same cache key.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an unambiguous key encoding, e.g. length-prefix or hash each component, or use a delimiter that is illegal in UIDs/actions, when composing userPermDenialCacheKey.
raw_findings.title: Underscore-delimited denial cache key is ambiguous for UIDs containing underscores
raw_findings.trigger: Grafana resource UIDs may legally contain underscores. A user is denied on (name="a_b", parent="c"), caching key "...action_a_b_c"; the same user then checks (name="a", parent="b_c"), which produces the identical key within the 30s TTL.

raw_findings.body: Previously one DB permission load served all subsequent denied checks via permCache for 30s; now each newly-denied resource triggers a full multi-query DB reload (singleflight only dedupes concurrent calls), amplifying DB load roughly N-fold for restricted users and enabling denial-of-service pressure on the permissions store.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Per-denied-resource DB query storm within each denial-cache TTL window, degrading DB and authz service latency under normal restricted-user browsing.
raw_findings.impact: Previously one DB permission load served all subsequent denied checks via permCache for 30s; now each newly-denied resource triggers a full multi-query DB reload (singleflight only dedupes concurrent calls), amplifying DB load roughly N-fold for restricted users and enabling denial-of-service pressure on the permissions store.
raw_findings.root_cause: The cache read at the top of getUserPermissions was removed and Check's cached-permissions path only returns early on allow, so every deny falls through to an unconditional DB permission fetch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Bound the requery amplification, e.g. cache a per-user "recently reloaded" marker or rate-limit the DB fallback after a cached deny, instead of unconditionally reloading permissions on every denied check for a new resource.
raw_findings.title: Removed permCache short-circuit makes every denied Check on an uncached resource perform a full DB permission reload
raw_findings.trigger: A user issues Check requests against many resources they lack access to (e.g., the frontend probing N dashboards). Each denied (name, parent) pair misses the per-resource denial cache the first time, and Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions -> getUserPermissions, which now always queries basic roles, teams, and permissions from the DB because the permCache read inside getUserPermissions was deleted.

raw_findings.body: permission_cache_usage{cache_hit="false"} is incremented even though the cache was hit, systematically understating the cache hit rate for users who are frequently denied and misleading operators monitoring the new caching behavior.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Metric label value contradicts actual cache behavior, corrupting cache-effectiveness observability.
raw_findings.impact: permission_cache_usage{cache_hit="false"} is incremented even though the cache was hit, systematically understating the cache hit rate for users who are frequently denied and misleading operators monitoring the new caching behavior.
raw_findings.root_cause: The single miss-counter increment placed after the cached block executes both on genuine cache misses and on cache hits that resulted in a deny.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Track whether getCachedIdentityPermissions returned a hit and increment the cache_hit="true" counter (or a distinct label such as "hit_denied") on the cached-but-denied path instead of falling into the miss counter.
raw_findings.title: Cache-hit-but-denied path in Check increments permission cache metric as a miss
raw_findings.trigger: A Check request finds the user's permissions in permCache (getCachedIdentityPermissions succeeds) but checkPermission returns allowed=false, so execution falls through past the cached block to line 137.

raw_findings.body: The test's stated purpose per its comment ("Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked") is not implemented — the map value is false, not true — so the test cannot detect a regression where the denial cache short-circuit is bypassed; it asserts a deny that would occur anyway.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test provides false assurance: it passes regardless of whether the new permDenialCache lookup is functioning.
raw_findings.impact: The test's stated purpose per its comment ("Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked") is not implemented — the map value is false, not true — so the test cannot detect a regression where the denial cache short-circuit is bypassed; it asserts a deny that would occur anyway.
raw_findings.root_cause: The seeded permission map grants nothing (value false), contradicting the accompanying comment and leaving the denial-cache precedence unverified.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set the permCache entry to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} (and/or seed fakeStore with an allowing permission) so the test only passes when the denial cache takes precedence.
raw_findings.title: Denial-cache test seeds a deny in permCache, so it passes even if the denial cache is ignored
raw_findings.trigger: Run TestService_CacheCheck subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" with the permDenialCache lookup in Check removed or broken: the seeded permCache entry (value false) and the empty fakeStore both independently produce a deny.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/readability degradation and unnecessary public API commitment.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that anonymous and renderer share the same UID '0' is speculative. validated_findings.trigger: Run TestService_CacheCheck subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" with the permDenialCache lookup in Check removed or broken: the seeded permCache entry (value false) and the empty fakeStore both independently produce a deny.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 982 shows permCache.Set with value 'map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}' but the comment on line 981 says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked'. The value 'false' means no permission, contradicting the comment's intent to grant permission. The test passes regardless of whether permDenialCache is checked because both caches deny access.

validated_findings.body: Expands the package's public API surface with an undocumented type and confusing receiver naming, violating Go naming/documentation conventions and inviting external dependence on an internal helper.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/readability degradation and unnecessary public API commitment.
validated_findings.impact: Expands the package's public API surface with an undocumented type and confusing receiver naming, violating Go naming/documentation conventions and inviting external dependence on an internal helper.
validated_findings.root_cause: New helper type was added exported and with receiver names copied from another cache implementation instead of following package conventions.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Unexport the type (noopCache) or add a doc comment explaining it disables client-side caching for the in-proc client, and rename method receivers from `lc` to `c`/`nc`.
validated_findings.title: Exported NoopCache lacks doc comment and uses misleading copy-paste receiver name
validated_findings.trigger: Code review / golint-style checks on package authz: NoopCache is exported but only used within this package, has no doc comment, and its methods use receiver name `lc` (apparently copied from a local-cache implementation).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a stylistic concern about exported type naming, documentation, and receiver naming conventions.
